statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of the public unauthenticated portal and representative reachable states; authenticated wagering functionality was not entered because no credentials were provided.

page.framework: ASP.NET Web Forms with jQuery 3.4.1 and Bootstrap 4.3.1
page.notes: Public login/marketing portal. Root redirects to Default8.aspx?lang=EN-US. Authenticated product was out of reach; popup endpoints returned minimal/blank responses when directly navigated.

checkOutcomes.method: Active evidence review using home-dark, home-desktop
checkOutcomes.evidence: Desktop and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are pixel-equivalent in treatment, while the page declares no color-scheme or theme media query.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the probe still found data-ride="carousel" and a deprecated <marquee>; neither was disabled.

checkOutcomes.method: Active evidence review using axe, home-high-contrast
checkOutcomes.evidence: axe measured 3.49:1 placeholder contrast for both login fields; forced-colors capture also leaves content-heavy raster imagery as the primary communication.
ShowGC() directly toggles table rows from displayed to none/table-row; no View Transition CSS or API use is present.
No scroll-linked animation or scroll handler is used, so the anti-pattern is absent.
No gesture-driven interaction is present to implement or fight with custom pointer handlers.
The audited portal has no meaningful scrolling chrome; no static sticky header or JS scroll toggle is present.
No tooltip, popover, or attached menu is present on the audited public surface.

checkOutcomes.method: Active evidence review using games-state, home-dom
checkOutcomes.evidence: The Games & Casino onclick state hides the main content and reveals a table row without moving focus, updating URL/state, or announcing the new section.
Load screenshot shows no modal, consent wall, or full-viewport interruption obscuring the portal.

checkOutcomes.method: Active evidence review using home-dom, platform-probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: DOM shows onclick div navigation and PopupCenter window calls, with zero dialog, popover, or details elements.
The entry screen keeps chrome compact and gives the primary viewport to service imagery and login.

checkOutcomes.method: Active evidence review using home-mobile, home-mobile-layout
checkOutcomes.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport Chrome reports no viewport meta and a 980 CSS-pixel layout scaled to 0.367; the screenshot renders login controls and text extremely small.

checkOutcomes.method: Active evidence review using home-dom, home-mobile
checkOutcomes.evidence: Rendered HTML uses a 975px table, 734px/233px columns, and many pixel widths; no container-query behavior was observed.

UFABET branding, betting categories, and the LOGIN action are visible in the first viewport.
Submitting test credentials navigated the inspected target away; the captured post-submit visual showed no inline validation or recovery affordance.
Invalid login produced no visible error in the captured state, and a missing route returned HTTP 403 with a blank-looking page.

paths.description: Public entry/login portal, the primary archetype and journey; tested visual, responsive, preference, accessibility, performance, security and invalid-login conditions.
Games & Casino in-page state, representing the only directly reachable stateful navigation surface.
Thai language variant, representing the 14-option localisation selector.
Betting Rules popup route, a distinct information surface; the endpoint rendered blank/minimal content in direct navigation.
Representative missing route to assess HTTP/network recovery behavior.

findings.summary: Theme is hard-coded rather than preference-aware.
findings.evidence: Desktop and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are pixel-equivalent in treatment, while the page declares no color-scheme or theme media query.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light and dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Auto-advancing motion ignores reduced-motion.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the probe still found data-ride="carousel" and a deprecated <marquee>; neither was disabled.
findings.suggestedFix: Stop carousel auto-advance and marquee motion under prefers-reduced-motion; retain manual controls.

findings.summary: Controls do not remain robust under contrast needs.
findings.evidence: axe measured 3.49:1 placeholder contrast for both login fields; forced-colors capture also leaves content-heavy raster imagery as the primary communication.
findings.suggestedFix: Use system colors in forced-colors and raise text/placeholder contrast to WCAG AA.

findings.summary: The in-page Games state swaps abruptly.
findings.evidence: ShowGC() directly toggles table rows from displayed to none/table-row; no View Transition CSS or API use is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the state change in document.startViewTransition with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: In-page navigation does not preserve or direct attention.
findings.evidence: The Games & Casino onclick state hides the main content and reveals a table row without moving focus, updating URL/state, or announcing the new section.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real link/button, update history, move focus to the section heading, and add a directional transition.

findings.summary: Navigation and overlays use ad-hoc scripting and popup windows.
findings.evidence: DOM shows onclick div navigation and PopupCenter window calls, with zero dialog, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace popup-window and clickable-div UI with semantic links/buttons and dialog/popover primitives where overlays are needed.

findings.summary: The mobile page is a scaled desktop canvas.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport Chrome reports no viewport meta and a 980 CSS-pixel layout scaled to 0.367; the screenshot renders login controls and text extremely small.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a standard viewport meta tag and rebuild the 975px table layout with fluid, intrinsic responsive CSS.

findings.summary: Components are fixed-width and cannot adapt to their containers.
findings.evidence: Rendered HTML uses a 975px table, 734px/233px columns, and many pixel widths; no container-query behavior was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace table layout with flexible components and use container queries where modules are reused.

findings.summary: Primary controls are too small for touch.
findings.evidence: The active controls measure only 20-22 CSS px high, including language, username, password, and Login.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44x44 CSS-pixel touch targets, preserve visible focus, and avoid hover-only/clickable-div actions.

findings.summary: The primary login flow does not expose a usable failure path.
findings.evidence: Submitting test credentials navigated the inspected target away; the captured post-submit visual showed no inline validation or recovery affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a semantic form submit and return an explicit, persistent, accessible error without losing page context.

findings.summary: Error and recovery states are missing.
findings.evidence: Invalid login produced no visible error in the captured state, and a missing route returned HTTP 403 with a blank-looking page.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide actionable inline errors, retry/help links, and branded 404/network failure pages with preserved navigation.

findings.summary: Throttled loading performance misses the Core Web Vitals bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse scored performance 0.54 with LCP 34.5s, TBT 310ms, and Speed Index 5.7s; the first-party trace measured LCP 1.78s without throttling.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP image, eliminate blocking chains, and verify under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Shipped scripting creates avoidable blocking under throttling.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 310ms TBT although the unthrottled trace saw no >50ms long task, indicating device/network sensitivity.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused libraries and defer or split non-critical work.

findings.summary: Five synchronous head scripts block parsing.
findings.evidence: HAR and DOM confirm jQuery, Popper, Bootstrap, bjqs and default.js are parser-inserted in <head> without async, defer, or module semantics.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary dependencies and defer the remaining scripts; keep only critical CSS in the initial path.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JS and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 345 KiB unused JavaScript and 51 KiB unused CSS; the HAR transfers 219,215 third-party bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit Bootstrap/jQuery/Popper usage, remove dead code, and load only the minimal component code required.

findings.summary: Core content and controls lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: axe found critical unnamed language select and image input, unnamed carousel controls, and the image audit found all 11 images missing alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add programmatic labels/names, meaningful alt text, and semantic controls.

findings.summary: Login placeholder text fails WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: axe measured 3.49:1 for the 11px username and password placeholders against white, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase foreground contrast and do not use placeholder text as the only label.

findings.summary: The document has no semantic structure and forces positive tabindex.
findings.evidence: axe found no main landmark, no h1, content outside landmarks, and tabindex values 1 and 3; the probe found no headings or landmarks.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce header/nav/main/footer and a logical heading hierarchy; use DOM order with tabindex=0 only.

findings.summary: Text is too small after mobile down-scaling.
findings.evidence: The 980px desktop layout is scaled to 36.7% on a 360px device, making 11-14px desktop text effectively tiny and difficult to read.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive typography and fluid layout without page-scale shrinkage.

findings.summary: The page fails mobile reflow and target sizing.
findings.evidence: No viewport meta is present, controls are 20-22px high, and the mobile screenshot is a miniature desktop page.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow normal user scaling, add viewport meta, reflow at 320 CSS px, and enlarge targets.

findings.summary: Document assets use brittle, legacy patterns.
findings.evidence: Images audit found 6 missing dimensions, all 11 in legacy PNG/JPG, 7 without responsive sources, and 5 below-fold images eagerly loaded; DOM is table-based.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic dimensions, responsive sources and modern formats, and use semantic CSS layout.

findings.summary: Deprecated and stale platform patterns remain.
findings.evidence: DOM includes deprecated <marquee>, javascript: links, popup windows, inline handlers, jQuery 3.4.1 and Bootstrap 4.3.1.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated elements/javascript URLs and update or replace legacy dependencies with platform primitives.

findings.summary: Metadata language does not match the visible English variant.
findings.evidence: The EN-US route has Thai title/description while the visible navigation and selected language are English.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide unique localized title and description matching each route language.

findings.summary: Navigation is not crawlable or mobile friendly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse crawlable-anchors failed; primary actions use javascript: and onclick divs, and viewport meta is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Use descriptive real href links and add a standard viewport declaration.

findings.summary: Public indexing signals are contradictory or absent.
findings.evidence: The public landing page declares noindex/googlebot noindex, has no canonical, and /sitemap.xml returns the text DIV rather than a sitemap.
findings.suggestedFix: Decide the indexing policy; if public, remove accidental noindex, add canonical URLs, and publish a valid sitemap.

findings.summary: The service has no structured or social metadata.
findings.evidence: Probe found zero JSON-LD and zero Open Graph tags despite the page representing a named betting service.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite structured data and Open Graph/Twitter metadata matching visible content.

findings.summary: Session transport defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP/HSTS/nosniff are absent and ASP.NET_SessionId lacks Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure, HttpOnly, and appropriate SameSite on session cookies; deploy HSTS, CSP, and nosniff.

findings.summary: Tracking loads before any visible consent or explanation.
findings.evidence: Tracker probe found Google Tag Manager and five third-party origins; HAR attributes 219,215 transferred bytes to third parties, with GTM the largest script at 139,430 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize analytics, gate non-essential tracking on informed consent, and self-host or remove unnecessary dependencies.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only and lacks modern assistance.
findings.evidence: The only auth fields are username/password; no WebAuthn/passkey surface was found, and autocomplete attributes are empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey/WebAuthn sign-in and retain properly annotated password fallback.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers probe found no frame protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP, HSTS, or nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP with frame-ancestors, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Core content disappears for non-JavaScript crawlers.
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetch received only 87 bytes of raw HTML with 0% rendered-word coverage; the crawler screenshot is blank while the browser screenshot has the portal.
findings.suggestedFix: Return meaningful server-rendered HTML and make links/forms work before JavaScript enhancement.

findings.summary: The app-like login portal has no install or offline support.
findings.evidence: Probe found no active service worker and recon found no web app manifest.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a manifest and service worker with an honest offline fallback for the shell and recovery guidance.

findings.summary: Failure routes do not provide recovery.
findings.evidence: A representative missing route returned HTTP 403 and a blank-looking screenshot with no navigation or retry guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve intentional 404/5xx/offline pages with clear status, navigation, and retry/help actions.

findings.summary: Language variants are not declared correctly.
findings.evidence: The page offers 14 language options but <html> has no lang or dir; axe flags html-has-lang.
findings.suggestedFix: Set accurate lang and dir per variant and use logical CSS properties for bidirectional layouts.

findings.summary: Date/time output is hard-coded rather than locale-aware.
findings.evidence: Inline code constructs serverTime from a locale-fragile string and renders a fixed DD-MM-YYYY time format on all variants.
findings.suggestedFix: Store an unambiguous timestamp and format with Intl.DateTimeFormat for the selected locale.

findings.summary: The displayed time assumes GMT+8 for every user.
findings.evidence: The header explicitly displays GMT+8 and the script seeds a naive Date without an offset, so interpretation varies by browser time zone.
findings.suggestedFix: Use ISO timestamps with offsets and render the user-selected or local zone with Intl.

findings.summary: Login errors are not handled humanely.
findings.evidence: The invalid-login capture contains no visible inline error, field state, help, or accessible announcement.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after submission and show a concise persistent error linked to the relevant fields and an aria-live summary.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields omit autocomplete semantics.
findings.evidence: The username and password inputs have empty autocomplete values and no labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Add visible labels and autocomplete="username" / "current-password"; support password managers and passkeys.

findings.summary: The account entry flow lacks recovery and safer authentication cues.
findings.evidence: The login view exposes only username, password, and Login: no password recovery/help route, passkey option, or visible security guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add findable account recovery/help and phishing-resistant sign-in while keeping commitments and account actions clear.

findings.summary: Images are eagerly delivered in legacy formats.
findings.evidence: All 11 images are JPG/PNG, 7 lack responsive sources, 5 below-fold images are not lazy, and all five carousel banners load up front.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert suitable assets to AVIF/WebP, add srcset/sizes, dimensions, and lazy-load non-current/below-fold images.

findings.summary: The idle page performs avoidable continuous work.
findings.evidence: Inline code starts a one-second setInterval for the clock, while Bootstrap auto-runs the carousel; hidden slides and legacy libraries are loaded immediately.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid continuous timers where possible, pause work when hidden/reduced-motion, and conditionally load interactive code.

findings.summary: Third-party and decorative media cost is disproportionate to the simple portal.
findings.evidence: HAR transfers 880,688 bytes: 634,658 image bytes and 219,215 third-party bytes; GTM alone is 139,430 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a page-weight budget, remove unused third parties, and defer non-current carousel/decorative media.

taskList.title: Rebuild the fixed 975px table page as a responsive, semantic layout
Fix accessible names, labels, landmarks, focus order, contrast and image alternatives
Harden session transport, cookies and browser security policies
Make login validation and failure recovery explicit and accessible
Remove parser-blocking legacy dependencies and unused code
Serve crawlable, progressively enhanced HTML with coherent indexing metadata
Add proper locale, direction, Intl formatting and timezone handling
Optimize and defer images, carousel motion and third-party resources
Modernize navigation and state transitions with semantic controls
Adopt preference-aware theming and stronger contrast behavior
Add an offline/install fallback appropriate to the portal
